Alice W: Hey @eng-platform — noticed traces start in api-prod but uploads-processor (background worker) is showing lots of orphan spans with no parent. Root span exists in API but worker spans have different trace IDs or none. Anyone seen trace context drop between HTTP handler -> enqueue -> worker?
Samir: Do you know which wire / queue you're using (Kafka/SQS) and the OTEL SDK version? Could be header propagation or instrumentation for executor/consumer.
Alice W: We use Kafka (topic uploads), opentelemetry-javaagent 1.28.0 attached to both services. SDK props: OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage. Worker uses Spring Boot + spring-kafka and a custom thread pool for processing.
Jen: Two quick checks: 1) Are the Kafka headers preserved by the producer/consumer? 2) Does the worker wrap the executor with the OTel context propagation? If you submit Runnables to an ExecutorService without context wrapper you'll lose the span.
Alice W: Logs from worker around the event: `2026-03-15T14:02:11Z WARN uploads-processor TraceContext missing parent traceId=none spanId=0000000000000000` — looks like headers aren't found at consumer time.
Samir: For spring-kafka we had to enable copyHeaders = true on the template and ensure the consumer doesn't strip unknown headers. Also Kafka header key for W3C is `traceparent` (lowercase) — check older producers using B3.
Jen: If you want a quick fix, wrap the ExecutorService with Context.current().wrap or use the opentelemetry-instrumentation-auto-instrumentation module that instruments Executor. Example:
```
ExecutorService delegate = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8);
ExecutorService ctxExec = Context.current().wrap(delegate);
// submit tasks to ctxExec so context propagates
```
Samir: Also confirm the propagators: `-Dotel.propagators=tracecontext` (or include `b3` if some services use B3). Mismatch between B3 and W3C will look like missing parent.
Alice W: Good call. Where's the best quick dashboard to confirm header propagation failures? I couldn't find a filter for "no-parent" spans.
Jen: Use the traces view in Console: https://console.redwood.ai/traces?service=uploads-processor and filter for span.duration>0 and `parent.span == null` (we have a saved query named "orphan-spans" under eng-platform). Also check the logs -> traceId mapping dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/logs?query=service:uploads-processor%20AND%20traceId:none
infra-bot: deploy-check: uploads-processor@prod v2.14 rolled 2026-03-15T13:50:00Z (no config changes to propagators).
Samir: If headers are missing in Kafka, instrument the producer side first. Run a local test producing a message and inspect headers via `kafka-console-consumer --property print.headers=true`. If the header isn't there, the consumer can't restore context.
Alice W: I ran the console consumer and the `traceparent` header is absent for ~30% of messages — looks like older service producing without OTEL.
Jen: Two options: 1) backfill: add a span attribute in worker when no traceparent to help triage; 2) default to creating a new root span but tag `sampling.reason=missing-propagation` so you can filter. I can open a tiny PR to add the tag + metrics.
Samir: Also consider setting `otel.instrumentation.messaging.experimental.receive-telemetry.enabled=true` for spring-kafka if you're on newer instrumentation.
Alice W: Thanks — I'll patch the producer to forward headers and enable the recv telemetry flag on worker. Jen, can you open the PR for the missing-propagation tag?
Jen: Yep — created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/uploads-processor/pull/58 (adds tag + metric + unit test).
Alice W: Awesome, testing now. I'll follow up once I verify traces show parent-child linking. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Reminder: there's a canary rolling for uploads-processor in prod; watch the canary dashboard if you retry tests.
Alice W: noted, pausing canary checks while I re-run local repros.
Samir: If you want, I can pair and run a producer that toggles B3 vs W3C to reproduce the ~30% drop. Ping when ready.
Alice W: Will do — pinging you when I have the repro.
Jen: TL;DR: check headers in Kafka, ensure propagators match across services, wrap executors or enable auto-instrumentation for async, add tag when propagation missing.
